reading.body:
CyrusOne's Cincinnati facility publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, making it the third-largest of only eight Ohio data centers with transparent power specs, holding 18 percent of the state's declared 60.4 MW.

Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities on record, but opacity is the norm: only eight publish IT capacity figures at all. This scarcity of disclosed power ratings means CIN2 belongs to a small set of sites where an operator's actual compute footprint is knowable. The state's total published capacity of 60.4 MW is modest compared to major compute hubs, though the true installed base may be larger if unmapped or undisclosed facilities exist.

The facility's 143,778 square feet at 11 MW translates to roughly 275 racks at typical AI training density. CIN2 carries compliance certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, positioning it for regulated workloads. An operator seeking east-of-Mississippi capacity with these credentials will find it accessible within a regional market where power constraints have not yet surfaced in public announcements.

Whether 11 MW matters depends on workload and tenant strategy. It is neither hyperscale nor negligible. The data does not reveal utilization, announced expansions, or whether Ohio's power grid has begun to constrain facility growth.
